title: Nobody can log in
summary: All login and token‑refresh requests began failing at ~06:00 UTC because the TLS server certificate presented by auth‑service expired at 2026‑10‑09T06:00:00Z. Edge‑gateway and auth‑service logs show a sudden burst of TLS handshake failures (“certificate notAfter …” and “remote error: tls: bad certificate”) exactly at that moment, and the edge‑gateway error rate jumped from ~0.2 % to >9 %. No downstream Redis errors were observed, confirming the failure originates at the TLS layer of auth‑service. The investigation concluded (conclusive) with high confidence (0.92) that the certificate expiry is the root cause; why the certificate was not renewed remains unverified.

hypothesis.mechanism: The TLS server certificate presented by auth-service expired at 2026-10-09T06:00:00Z. After that moment every new TLS handshake from edge-gateway fails with “certificate notAfter 2026-10-09T06:00:00Z” (edge-gateway logs) and “remote error: tls: bad certificate” (auth-service logs). The handshake failures appear on both sides at 06:00:06‑06:00:09 and the edge-gateway error_rate jumps from 0.2 % to >4 % (last 9.6 %). No downstream Redis errors are observed, confirming the failure originates at the TLS layer of auth-service.
predictions: No successful TLS handshakes to auth-service after 06:00:00Z until the certificate is renewed.

hypothesis.mechanism: The only recorded change before the outage is chg:2541 (05:52:30 UTC) which raised upstream.keepalive_timeout_s from 60 s to 75 s. A longer keep‑alive can keep idle TLS connections in the gateway’s connection pool past the certificate expiry moment (06:00 UTC). When the pool later re‑uses those stale connections, the server presents an already‑expired certificate, causing a burst of handshake failures that surface as 5xx on /v1/session.
predictions: Edge-gateway connection-pool metrics show a rise in reused-connection handshake failures after 06:00.
If the keep-alive timeout were reverted to 60 s, the failure burst would disappear (or be delayed).

objections.detail: No edge‑gateway TLS connection‑pool metrics (idle count, handshake‑success vs reuse) are available for 05:50‑06:10 UTC (GAP‑13). Without them we cannot confirm that longer keep‑alive caused reuse of expired‑cert connections.
HYP‑1 (certificate expiry) fully explains the observed handshake failures and error‑rate spike. Until HYP‑2 demonstrates a distinct contribution, it remains an unruled‑out alternative.

hypothesis.mechanism: An automated certificate-management component (e.g., cert-manager, Vault, external CA) failed to renew the auth-service TLS certificate before its notAfter = 06:00 UTC. The failure is invisible in the change census because it is not a user‑initiated config change. The expiry then produces the same TLS‑handshake failure pattern as H1.
predictions: Cert-manager or secret-controller logs show a renewal attempt that did not complete before 06:00 UTC.
A new certificate appears in the auth-service secret after the outage is mitigated.

objections.detail: Assertion that a certificate‑management component failed to renew the cert has no log or metric support (GAP‑15).

Edge‑gateway forwards /v1/session traffic to auth‑service via a hard HTTP dependency with a 1 000 ms timeout (dep:edge-gateway→auth-service).
The changed keep‑alive timeout governs idle connection reuse and does not modify request routing, auth‑header processing, or the request timeout.

assumptions.statement: The certificate’s notAfter value is exactly 2026-10-09T06:00:00Z (as logged by edge-gateway).
assumptions.reason: Edge-gateway logs explicitly cite certificate notAfter 2026-10-09T06:00:00Z.

assumptions.statement: Edge-gateway validates notAfter on every new handshake (standard TLS behaviour).
assumptions.reason: TLS libraries verify expiration on each full handshake.

assumptions.statement: No auth-service deploy / config / secret-rotation occurred between 05:15‑06:25 UTC.
assumptions.reason: Change census shows zero events for auth-service in that window (OBS-9).

assumptions.statement: Edge-gateway’s HTTP client re-uses a TLS session without performing a fresh handshake when a keep-alive connection is taken from the pool (session‑ticket / session‑ID resumption).
assumptions.reason: Required for the keep-alive change to cause reuse of an expired cert.

assumptions.statement: The keep-alive increase caused a measurable number of connections opened before 06:00 to stay alive after 06:00.
assumptions.reason: Only then would stale connections be reused after expiry.

assumptions.statement: The gateway does not validate notAfter on resumed sessions (unlikely for standard libraries).
assumptions.reason: Otherwise resumed sessions would also fail, which is not indicated.

assumptions.statement: The certificate is managed by an external controller not represented in the change census.
assumptions.reason: Explains absence of a recorded change while cert expired.

assumptions.statement: The controller attempted renewal but the new cert was not deployed to auth-service pods before 06:00.
assumptions.reason: Would produce the observed expiry without a visible config change.

actions.description: Renew the auth‑service TLS certificate immediately and roll it out to all pods.
actions.rationale: The expired certificate is the direct cause of the handshake failures and the login outage.

actions.description: Repair or reconfigure the certificate‑management automation (e.g., cert‑manager/Vault) so that certificates are renewed well before their notAfter date.
actions.rationale: The certificate was allowed to expire, indicating a failure in the renewal process.

actions.description: Add monitoring and alerting on TLS certificate expiry (e.g., cert‑exporter alerts 30 days, 7 days, 1 day before expiry) and on auth‑service TLS handshake error rates.
actions.rationale: Early detection will prevent a repeat outage caused by an unnoticed expiry.

actions.description: Examine cert‑manager / secret‑controller logs and the auth‑service secret history to determine why the renewal did not complete before 06:00 UTC.
actions.rationale: The root cause of the expiry (HYP‑3) is still unknown; logs were not captured (GAP‑15).

open_questions: Why did the certificate‑management component fail to renew the auth‑service TLS certificate before its notAfter timestamp?
Whether the edge‑gateway keep‑alive timeout increase (chg:2541) contributed to the failure burst (insufficient TLS connection‑pool metrics – GAP‑13).
What caused the missing log shards for az‑b (GAP‑11, GAP‑12, GAP‑16) and could they contain additional clues?
